documents.title: Artificial Intelligence at Portland State University
documents.summary: Provost-office AI page lists guiding principles (human oversight, equity, literacy, academic freedom, transparency, shared responsibility) and links to student, teaching and research resources. Course rules are left to instructors.
documents.stance_why: The page sets university principles that embrace AI and says "Expectations for the acceptable use of AI in a course are determined by the instructor"; it sets no default rule, so delegates.

units.why: The opening sentence sets the university-wide posture: the working group "embraces responsible use" of AI as a tool for teaching, learning and research. It is an institution-level framework statement, so P56 fits better than P02, which is a course default rule.
units.anchor: embraces responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI) as a transformative tool
units.frag_start: Portland State University's AI Working Group
units.fit_note: Also welcomes AI use, which P56 does not capture.

units.why: "critical evaluations, final decisions, and ethical judgments are made by people, not algorithms" keeps people responsible for decisions; P73 fits since it is not limited to grading (P46).
units.anchor: critical evaluations, final decisions, and ethical judgments are made by people, not algorithms

units.why: "ensuring that AI adoption does not widen the digital divide" together with providing "equitable access to tools" is an equity commitment, matching P51.
units.anchor: ensuring that AI adoption does not widen the digital divide

units.why: "critically evaluate AI systems for biases" is a commitment to examine bias in AI, which is P53 (the access half of the sentence is coded as P51).
units.anchor: critically evaluate AI systems for biases

units.why: "PSU is committed to fostering AI literacy across the institution" for students, faculty and staff is institution-wide AI-literacy provision, P70 (not faculty-only P63).
units.anchor: committed to fostering AI literacy across the institution

units.why: "faculty have the autonomy to determine if and how AI tools are integrated into their teaching and research" hands the decision to instructors, so P04.
units.anchor: faculty have the autonomy to determine if and how AI tools are integrated

units.why: "a culture of experimentation and exploration ... rather than one of restriction" prefers encouraging AI over restricting it; P02 fits, although it is a culture statement and not a default rule for coursework.
units.anchor: We encourage a culture of experimentation and exploration of ways AI can improve learning
units.fit_note: Phrased as a university culture preference, not a default rule for coursework.

units.why: "We expect transparency from all members of our community regarding the use of AI" and "acknowledging AI's role in the generative process" is a general disclosure expectation, nearest P24; it is not tied to a submission.
units.anchor: We expect transparency from all members of our community regarding the use of AI
units.fit_note: Applies to everyone in academic and professional work and to administrative decisions, not only to a student submission.

units.why: "the individual remains accountable for the accuracy, attribution, and ethical impact of their output" makes each person responsible for what they submit even if AI assists; P29.
units.anchor: the individual remains accountable for the accuracy, attribution, and ethical impact of their output

units.why: "Expectations for the acceptable use of AI in a course are determined by the instructor and may differ from class to class" delegates the rule to instructors: P04.
units.anchor: Expectations for the acceptable use of AI in a course are determined by the instructor

units.why: "Students should check with their instructors and read the syllabi to learn to what extent AI tools can be used" tells students where to find the rule; P10 (ask first) is nearest.
units.anchor: Students should check with their instructors and read the syllabi
units.fit_note: Also tells students to read the syllabus, not only to ask.

units.why: "PSU ... expects students to use AI tools responsibly and ethically" is a general principle about AI and academic integrity, matching the framework type P56.
units.anchor: expects students to use AI tools responsibly and ethically

units.why: The Library "offers guidance on citation styles for generative AI" so students can "credit sources accurately"; it points to citing AI, nearest P24, but is a resource not a requirement.
units.anchor: The PSU Library offers guidance on citation styles for generative AI
units.fit_note: Only points to library citation guidance; does not state that citation is required.

units.why: "Faculty and students involved in research ... are encouraged to explore AI's potential while adhering to ethical standards" governs AI in research, P62.
units.anchor: Faculty and students involved in research at PSU are encouraged to explore

units.why: The security resource gives "guidance on protecting personal data when using AI applications like ChatGPT, Copilot"; this is data protection advice, P50.
units.anchor: guidance on protecting personal data when using AI applications like ChatGPT, Copilot

units.why: "PSU provides faculty, staff, and students with access to a suite of generative AI tools, including Google's Gemini and NotebookLM" is a sanctioned institution-provided tool: P17.
units.anchor: PSU provides faculty, staff, and students with access to a suite of generative AI tools

units.why: "When using or procuring AI tools, please be sure to follow PSU's guidelines and policies" requires compliance with existing university policy: P77.
units.anchor: When using or procuring AI tools, please be sure to follow

units.why: The Office of Academic Innovation "offers AI teaching resources and support consultations to all educators", plus workshops and the InnovAIte Academy; support for faculty learning AI is P63.
units.anchor: offers AI teaching resources and support consultations to all educators at PSU

units.why: "This sample syllabus language helps faculty communicate AI policies effectively" supports syllabus statements, nearest P09, but offers sample text and does not require a statement.
units.anchor: This sample syllabus language helps faculty communicate AI policies effectively
units.fit_note: Provides optional sample language; does not mandate a syllabus statement.

units.why: The research guide stresses "transparency, privacy, and the importance of professional integrity" for AI in research; research-specific, so P62 not P56.
units.anchor: emphasizing transparency, privacy, and the importance of professional integrity

units.why: A cross-functional working group is "tasked with recommending AI guidance and tools", naming who maintains the guidance; closest is P56 (institution-level framework).
units.anchor: tasked with recommending AI guidance and tools
units.fit_note: Describes who maintains the guidance (governance), not the principles themselves.

documents.title: Academic Misconduct (incl. 'Academic Misconduct and AI')
documents.summary: Dean of Student Life page explains that unauthorized AI use falls under the Code's cheating and plagiarism rules, requires authorization and citation, and gives faculty advice on syllabus clarity, assignments and detectors.
documents.stance_why: The page says the Code does not explicitly prohibit AI but that use "without prior explicit authorization from the instructor" is a potential violation. AI is therefore barred unless the instructor permits it, which is restrict.

units.why: "students should be cautious about the use of AI for academic work" discourages AI without banning it, which is P03.
units.anchor: students should be cautious about the use of AI for academic work

units.why: "the expectation under our Code is that work students submit is their own original work, completed without the use of unauthorized materials and tools" requires ownership of submitted work: P29.
units.anchor: work students submit is their own original work, completed without the use of unauthorized materials

units.why: Quoting section 9, "all submissions ... must either be the Student's own work, or must clearly acknowledge the source(s)" requires acknowledging non-own work; "Unless otherwise specified by the faculty member" lets instructors vary it. P24 fits the acknowledgement duty.
units.anchor: must either be the Student's own work, or must clearly acknowledge the source(s)
units.fit_note: General Code rule on acknowledging sources, applied to AI; does not mention AI itself.

units.why: "While the code doesn't explicitly prohibit AI technology, it does prohibit cheating, the use of unauthorized materials ... which would include tools like AI generators" classifies AI misuse as existing misconduct: P36.
units.anchor: it does prohibit cheating, the use of unauthorized materials in the general sense

units.why: "the use of AI ... without prior explicit authorization from the instructor assigning the work, would be considered a potential violation" sets the fallback: AI is not allowed unless the instructor authorizes it. P06 fits better than P36 because the point is the default absent permission; referral is coded separately.
units.anchor: without prior explicit authorization from the instructor assigning the work, would be considered a potential
units.frag_start: Please know, the use of AI

units.why: The same sentence says such use "would be referred to the Director of Student Conduct and Conflict Resolution for review and possible disciplinary action", an enforcement route: P36.
units.anchor: would be referred to the Director of Student Conduct and Conflict Resolution for review
units.frag_start: Please know, the use of AI

units.why: "you would need to properly cite the sources of that work to give appropriate attribution" requires citing AI generators used: P24.
units.anchor: you would need to properly cite the sources of that work
units.frag_start: If you do use materials and

units.why: "they should be used as specified in the assignment instructions" makes the assignment the place where permitted AI use is defined: P04.
units.anchor: they should be used as specified in the assignment instructions

units.why: "If you have questions about the use of any resources and materials ... check with your instructor" tells students to ask first: P10.
units.anchor: If you have questions about the use of any resources and materials

units.why: "use the library, or reach out to the Writing Center" directs students to human support, P72; the instructor part of the sentence is coded as P10.
units.anchor: use the library, or reach out to the

units.why: Students "have the opportunity to participate in the review process, share your perspective, and provide any information/documentation"; this lets accused students respond, P64, though it is not specific to AI.
units.anchor: you have the opportunity to participate in the review process, share your perspective
units.frag_start: If you have received an email
units.frag_end: will not be penalized for not participating.

units.why: The conduct review list gives students "Notice of the report, allegations", "Opportunity to appeal the outcome" and "A right to privacy"; fairness in integrity cases, P64.
units.anchor: Opportunity to appeal the outcome
units.frag_start: In the Conduct Review process, the

units.why: "The student should be made aware of the situation ... outline how you came to the conclusion of academic dishonesty" tells faculty to talk with the student first: P57.
units.anchor: The student should be made aware of the situation.
units.fit_note: Applies to academic dishonesty in general, not only AI.

units.why: "Give a proper grade ... In most cases, this will be a 0 or F" and not "an automatic F for the entire course" states penalty norms: P37.
units.anchor: Give a proper grade for the assignment or exam in question.
units.fit_note: Applies to academic dishonesty in general; also caps the penalty and separates grading from conduct.

units.why: "Report the matter to the Conduct Office" tells instructors to route suspected dishonesty to the conduct process; P36.
units.anchor: Report the matter to the Conduct Office.

units.why: "Consider in advance whether you will allow the use of AI programs in your course" leaves the decision to each instructor: P04.
units.anchor: Consider in advance whether you will allow the use of AI programs in your course.

units.why: "If you choose not to allow AI programs, be clear about this in the syllabus and discuss it at the start of the term" asks for a syllabus statement: P09.
units.anchor: clear about this in the syllabus and discuss it at the start of the term
units.fit_note: Conditional on choosing to ban AI; the allow case asks to clarify expectations.

units.why: "clarify the expectations around the proper use, limitations on assignments, and any pitfalls" asks instructors to explain their rules: P66 fits (reasons and discussion), beyond P09.
units.anchor: clarify the expectations around the proper use, limitations on assignments, and any pitfalls

units.why: "Talk with students about both the potential and pitfalls in AI generators" is a call to discuss AI in class: P66.
units.anchor: Talk with students about both the potential and pitfalls in AI generators.

units.why: "updating assignment structures and prompts to avoid them being easily solved/written by AI" redesigns assignments around AI: P35.
units.anchor: updating assignment structures and prompts to avoid them being easily solved/written by AI

units.why: "Become familiar with a few AI generators" so faculty can see responses; faculty are urged to learn the tools, P63, although it also serves identifying AI work.
units.anchor: Become familiar with a few AI generators.
units.fit_note: Aims at learning the tools in order to recognise AI-generated student work.

units.why: "Many of the programs are new, inaccurate, or ineffective. Do not rely entirely on these programs" warns against detector reliance: P39.
units.anchor: Do not rely entirely on these programs to determine the use of AI.

documents.title: CS Graduate Student Handbook 2025-26 (section 11.8)
documents.summary: One sentence in the CS graduate handbook says the department follows the university misconduct rules and that generative-AI rules differ by course, pointing students to syllabi.
documents.stance_why: The single AI sentence says the CS department follows university rules and that "the use of generative AI may differ widely among CS courses"; it sets no rule itself and defers to syllabi, so delegates.

units.why: "The CS department follows the university's general rules on academic misconduct" ties the department to the university process: P36 nearest.
units.anchor: The CS department follows the university's general rules on
units.fit_note: Does not mention AI; defers to the university rules.

units.why: "the use of generative AI may differ widely among CS courses" says each course sets its own rules. P11 fits better than P04 because the point is that rules vary by course, not who decides.
units.anchor: the use of generative AI may differ widely among CS courses

units.why: "they should consult the course syllabus for more detailed information" sends students to the syllabus: P10 (nearest) since no ask-first duty is stated.
units.anchor: should consult the course syllabus for more detailed information.
units.fit_note: Points to the syllabus, not to asking the instructor.

notes: Course syllabi deferred in the collect file. Document 2 is a general academic-misconduct page; several faculty-process and student-rights units are not AI-specific and carry fit_notes.
